column1: # The layers of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 3, one row per first-party crate (a workspace member
# whose directory is under crates/; the vendored crates under vendor/ are not first-party).
# scripts/ci/check-crate-edges.ps1 requires every normal and build dependency between two first-party
# crates, target-specific tables included, to go from a higher layer to a lower one; a same-layer or
# upward edge passes only as a row of scripts/ci/crate-edge-exemptions.tsv. A first-party crate with
# no row here fails the gate, and so does a row naming no first-party crate: a new crate is placed on
# purpose. Dev-dependencies are not layer edges: they are not in the shipped graph, and Cargo allows
# them in both directions (bt-platform and bt-pty each name the other as one; bt-pty naming bt-term
# only as a dev-dependency is ARCHITECTURE section 3.2's repair of D-13).
# 0  no first-party dependency: the Unicode tables, the layout solver, SHA-256 and the release format;
#    bt-effects, the admission vocabulary and the file-read ledger every layer above names (std and
# 1  bt-transcript (the text model); bt-workbench, which depends on bt-layout and on nothing that
#    reads a window, a clock, a file or the platform
# 3  detection and the viewport over documents
# 4  bt-term and bt-platform, one layer: neither names the other, and the host installs into
#    bt-term what the platform layer answers (section 3.2; structural-debt D-14, repaid)
# 5  bt-render and bt-math (over bt-effects, not the platform), persistence and the PTY transport;
#    bt-term's dependency on bt-math goes upward and is recorded debt (section 3.2, structural-debt D-15)
# 6  bt-compose, the composition order and the math execution over bt-term, bt-viewport, bt-render
#    and bt-math (layers 3-5): above every crate it orders and below the one host that lends it
# 7  bt-app; bt-corpus and bt-lint-probe, tools nothing depends on; bt-source, which only tests read
